summary: Diagnosed likely masking as Unreal auto exposure / eye adaptation normalizing perceived brightness after scene-light intensity scaling. Added launch-time fixed-exposure control to both flashlight entry points, defaulting to disabled auto exposure for flashlight validation with explicit --enable-auto-exposure opt-out.
work_completed: Added --disable-auto-exposure / --enable-auto-exposure mutually exclusive CLI flags to examples/flashlight/run.py; default is --disable-auto-exposure.

Added --disable-auto-exposure / --enable-auto-exposure mutually exclusive CLI flags to examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py; default is --disable-auto-exposure for both teleop and render modes.

Added renderer INI launch overrides when auto exposure is disabled: r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure=False and r.EyeAdaptationQuality=0, while preserving any existing SP_CORE CONFIG_ENGINE_INI_STRING content.
Refactored examples/flashlight/run.py config construction into build_config(args, user_config_files=None) so exposure config can be tested without launching Unreal.

Kept scene-light scaling order intact: both entry points still disable or scale existing scene lights inside the first begin_frame before spawning the co-located flashlight, so the spawned flashlight intensity is not scaled.
Updated tests/test_orbit_collection_validation.py with defaults, explicit enable/disable parsing, mutually exclusive flag rejection, and config INI validation for the new exposure controls.
Updated examples/flashlight/README.md with fixed-exposure explanation and commands comparing --scene-light-intensity-scale values 0.2, 0.1, and 0.0.

findings.message: Likely cause: scene light components were scaled, but Unreal's eye adaptation could compensate exposure frame-to-frame so 0.2, 0.1, and 0.0 scene-light scales looked similarly bright in the final tone-mapped view.
